# HYP-04 Independent R-Reference Validation v1.0 (DRAFT)

> **Satisfies D10 of the HYP-04 analysis lock (Authoritative CR2 implementation). No statistical method is approved, no gate condition changes, and this is not evidence that supply-chain transmission exists.**
>
> Phase 2's preregistration lock (`HYP04_PHASE2_LOCK_2026-09-10.json`) remains signed and unchanged. This validation moves no gate condition and touches no frozen or holdout event.

**Synthetic data only.** No observation, event, outcome, panel, or market value was read. Every number below comes from fixtures generated by the committed `fixtures.py::make_fixture` seed (`20260910`), and no real ticker or canonical-artifact path appears anywhere in the interchange file.

Machine-readable companion: [`HYP04_R_REFERENCE_VALIDATION_v1.0.json`](HYP04_R_REFERENCE_VALIDATION_v1.0.json).

---

## 1. What D10 required, and what this closes

The HYP-04 analysis lock's D10 states that no Phase 3 (holdout) result may be produced before an R cross-check exists, modelled on `tools/hyp01_r_reference/` — "a blocking failure, not a deferrable TODO."

**The underlying CR2/Satterthwaite arithmetic did not need re-validation.** `hyp04_supply_chain_hedge/clustered_se.py`'s own docstring states its `cr_vcov` and `satterthwaite_df` are mirrored verbatim from `tools/hyp01_inference_feasibility.py` — the exact functions the HYP-01 R cross-check already validated against clubSandwich (13/13 fixtures, commit `97705ed`). What D10 actually required was proof that HYP-04's own *usage* of that arithmetic — its own 3-column design matrix (intercept, shock magnitude, days-to-peer-earnings) and its own `calendar_period` clustering (D1) — reproduces correctly. That is what this validation checks, and it is what was missing.

## 2. How the two implementations were made to see the same numbers

The fixtures are **not** regenerated in R. There is one generator — `make_fixture` in `tools/hyp04_r_reference/fixtures.py`, purpose-built for this bridge — and R consumes its output:

1. `export_fixtures.py` serialises all 14 fixtures to a strict-JSON interchange file carrying only the outcome vector, design matrix, coefficient names, cluster labels, target coefficient, fixture id and expected refusal status.
2. Missing values are encoded as JSON `null`, never as a sentinel number.
3. Each fixture carries a SHA-256 over a **language-neutral canonical string**. R rebuilds that string from the values it parsed and recomputes the digest independently. **All 14 verified.**
4. Numeric results travel back as `%.17g` **strings**, not JSON numbers, so the comparison measures the computation rather than jsonlite's ~15-significant-digit writer.
5. The Python side is recomputed by calling `hyp04_supply_chain_hedge.clustered_se.cr_vcov` / `satterthwaite_df` **directly** — the actual production module, not a copy of it, hash-pinned in the artifact (`production_module_sha256`).

## 3. Specification — resolved explicitly, not left to defaults

Identical to `tools/hyp01_r_reference`'s specification (intercept handling, coefficient/cluster ordering, `na.action = na.fail`, CR2 leverage adjustment, identity working model, matrix tolerance) — see that bridge's report for the full table; nothing here differs, because `cr2_reference.R` is the same script with only the schema name changed. `inverse_var` sensitivity was likewise checked both ways on every fixture.

## 4. Result — 8 of 9 admissible fixtures match; 5 refuse identically; 1 is a genuine, reported behaviour difference

**The supported claim is two-part, and the parts must not be merged:**

> HYP-04's production CR2 covariance, standard-error, t-statistic, and p-value outputs (`hyp04_supply_chain_hedge.clustered_se`, on HYP-04's own 3-column design matrix and `calendar_period` clustering) agree with clubSandwich on HYP-04's own synthetic fixture matrix, under tolerances reused verbatim from HYP-01's PR #17. The continuous Satterthwaite degrees of freedom agree under the tolerance reused verbatim from HYP-01's PR #18. **Neither tolerance was preregistered specifically for HYP-04; both are reused by citation because the underlying arithmetic is identical mirrored code.**

Neither tolerance set was loosened, reinterpreted, or replaced. Classification: **`MATCH_WITHIN_TOLERANCES_REUSED_FROM_HYP01_PR17_AND_PR18`**.

| Field | Worst absolute difference | Worst relative difference | Tolerance and its provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coefficients | 7.216 × 10⁻¹⁶ | 2.044 × 10⁻¹⁵ | reused PR #17: rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-12 |
| CR2 covariance matrix | 8.327 × 10⁻¹⁶ | 1.008 × 10⁻¹⁴ | reused PR #17: rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-12 |
| Target variance | 3.192 × 10⁻¹⁶ | 9.576 × 10⁻¹⁵ | reused PR #17: rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-12 |
| Standard error | 8.882 × 10⁻¹⁶ | 4.865 × 10⁻¹⁵ | reused PR #17: rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-12 |
| t-statistic | 2.665 × 10⁻¹⁵ | 6.689 × 10⁻¹⁶ | reused PR #17: rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-11 |
| p-value | 8.882 × 10⁻¹⁶ | 1.030 × 10⁻¹⁵ | reused PR #17: rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-12 |
| **Satterthwaite df** | 4.174 × 10⁻¹⁴ | 8.039 × 10⁻¹⁵ | **reused PR #18 tolerance — NOT preregistered for HYP-04** (see §5) |

Agreement is at the floating-point noise floor, several orders of magnitude inside every tolerance — including on **G03, the purpose-built thin/singleton-cluster fixture** (8 `calendar_period` clusters, 7 of them singletons, matching what the committed Phase 1 diagnostic actually showed at horizon 20), which is the specific regime a HYP-01-shaped fixture set would never have exercised.

## 5. The Satterthwaite-df tolerance is reused, not preregistered for HYP-04

HYP-01's PR #17 tolerance set defines degrees of freedom as `exact_integer_equality`, written for CR1's integer *G* − 1; it cannot express agreement on the continuous Satterthwaite df. HYP-01's own PR #18 prespecified a separate tolerance (rtol 1e-8, atol 1e-10) for exactly this reason. **This validation reuses that PR #18 number verbatim rather than prespecifying a third one for HYP-04**, because the arithmetic under test is the identical mirrored code — inventing a different tolerance for identical arithmetic would imply a difference that does not exist.

This is a deliberate departure from the "preregister everything specifically for this study" pattern, and it is labelled as such everywhere: `tolerance_provenance.preregistered_specifically_for_hyp04` is `false`, and the field-level tag is `PR18_REUSED`, not `PR18`. **The df row above is evidence gathered under a reused HYP-01 rule. It is not a claim that HYP-04 preregistered its own tolerance, and must never be described as such.**

## 6. Refusal and behaviour-difference fixtures

| Fixture | Python | clubSandwich / `lm` | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| `G04_near_collinear_full_rank` | `ILL_CONDITIONED_DESIGN` | aliased coefficient `days_to_peer_earnings` | `REFUSED_BY_BOTH` |
| `G05_exactly_rank_deficient` | `RANK_DEFICIENT_DESIGN` | aliased coefficient | `REFUSED_BY_BOTH` |
| `G06_zero_variance_control` | `ZERO_VARIANCE_PREDICTOR` | aliased coefficient | `REFUSED_BY_BOTH` |
| `G07_missing_value` | `NONFINITE_VALUE_PRESENT` | `na.fail`: missing values in object | `REFUSED_BY_BOTH` |
| `G08_below_min_two_clusters` | `FEWER_THAN_TWO_CLUSTERS` | R error (single-level factor) | `REFUSED_BY_BOTH` |
| `G10_perfect_fit` | `DEGENERATE_FIT_RESIDUAL_VARIANCE_AT_NOISE_FLOOR` | **computes** | `REFERENCE_BEHAVIOR_DIFFERENCE` |

Five fixtures refuse on both sides; the stated reasons are not identical, which is not a defect — the two implementations reach the same refusal through different diagnostics (Python screens condition number / column variance / residual variance explicitly; R discovers the same degeneracies as aliased coefficients or a fitting error).

**`G10_perfect_fit` is a genuine behaviour difference, reported as one, matching the same finding HYP-01's own bridge made on its analogous fixture (`F08_perfect_fit`).** Python refuses by a prespecified relative-residual-variance threshold; R computes a number. Neither side was adjusted. On this fixture HYP-04's Python output is simply not validated, because there is nothing meaningful to validate it against.

## 7. What is still not validated by this cross-check

- **Max-T multiplicity correction is out of scope.** D10's own title is "Authoritative CR2 implementation"; max-T is pure Python order-statistics over already-computed t-statistics, and clubSandwich implements no equivalent to check it against. This validation covers CR2 + Satterthwaite only, the same scope HYP-01's bridge used.
- **CR3 and the wild cluster bootstrap** remain unvalidated in this repository, as they were before this work — HYP-04 does not use either.
- **This is not a finding.** It does not say supply-chain transmission exists, that the shock-magnitude coefficient is meaningful, or that Phase 3 will produce a significant result. It says HYP-04's CR2/Satterthwaite code, exercised on its own design and clustering, computes what clubSandwich computes.

## 8. What this evidence does and does not support

Supported, exactly — both sentences are required:

> **HYP-04's production CR2 covariance, standard-error, t-statistic, and p-value outputs agree with clubSandwich on HYP-04's own synthetic fixture matrix, under tolerances reused verbatim from HYP-01's PR #17. The continuous Satterthwaite degrees of freedom agree under the tolerance reused verbatim from HYP-01's PR #18. Neither tolerance was preregistered specifically for HYP-04; both are reused by citation because the underlying arithmetic is identical mirrored code.**

D10 is satisfied on that basis.

Not supported, and not claimed anywhere in this validation:

- that supply-chain transmission exists, or that any HYP-04 coefficient is meaningful;
- that CR2 is scientifically optimal, or approved, selected, or production-eligible;
- that Phase 3 will produce a significant result, or that the study is adequately powered;
- that any gate condition changed — the gate reads exactly as it did before this work: OPEN, 0 denials, 214 frozen events;
- anything at all about real data — none was read.

## 9. Reproducing this

```
python tools/hyp04_r_reference/run_validation.py --out <artifact.json>
```

One command: export fixtures, run the R reference, recompute the Python side, compare, write the artifact, exit nonzero on any unexplained mismatch. R and its packages are installed beforehand per [`r-packages.lock.json`](../tools/hyp04_r_reference/r-packages.lock.json) — same R 4.6.1, same 10 packages as `tools/hyp01_r_reference` (no new dependency was needed); the validation itself makes no network request.

**A reproducibility note surfaced while building this lockfile, worth recording plainly.** Re-downloading the identical pinned package set from the identical dated CRAN snapshot URL (`packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2026-08-11`), roughly one month after `tools/hyp01_r_reference`'s own install, produced the **same versions** (verified with `numeric_version()`) but **different bytes** on every one of the 10 packages. Version pinning held; byte-level pinning of a dated snapshot over time did not. This is recorded in `r-packages.lock.json`'s `observed_snapshot_binary_instability` field rather than silently reused or explained away — no cause was investigated beyond confirming the version and package name are unchanged.

`test_hyp04_supply_chain_hedge_r_reference.py` executes this bridge and recomputes the comparison rather than reading the artifact's declarations. Where R is unavailable it verifies everything that does not require it and says plainly which assertions were skipped. CI (`.github/workflows/hyp04-r-reference-validation.yml`) additionally runs `verify_artifact.py`, which re-checks a freshly computed result against this committed artifact across every material field, using documented tolerances for continuous quantities (CI runs a different OS, R build and BLAS) and exact equality for discrete ones.
